name: Shallum
title: Israel's Brief Reigning King
summary: Shallum, son of Jabesh, was one of the shortest-reigning kings in the northern kingdom of Israel. He seized power by assassinating King Zechariah and ruled for only one month in Samaria before being killed himself by Menahem, son of Gadi. His brief reign illustrates the political instability and violence that characterized the final decade of the northern kingdom.

keyEvents.title: Conspiracy Against King Zechariah
keyEvents.description: Shallum conspired against King Zechariah, son of Jeroboam II, killed him publicly, and thus took the throne of Israel.

keyEvents.title: Ascended to Israel's Throne
keyEvents.description: After the murder of Zechariah, Shallum became king over Israel in Samaria, but his reign lasted only one month.

keyEvents.title: Fulfillment of the Lord's Word to Jehu
keyEvents.description: The fall of Zechariah and Shallum's rise to power marked the end of Jehu's dynasty, which the Lord had promised would sit on Israel's throne for four generations.

keyEvents.title: Menahem Rises Against Shallum
keyEvents.description: Menahem, son of Gadi, went up from Tirzah to Samaria and struck Shallum down and became king in his place.

keyEvents.title: Summary of Shallum's brief reign
keyEvents.description: Shallum's reign of only one month is among the shortest in the Bible and testifies to the chaotic political situation in the final days of the Northern Kingdom.
